title: Optimizing Legacy Monorepo Frontend Iteration
business: A mid-sized enterprise managing a complex internal dashboard suite composed of multiple legacy React modules.
problem: The existing build pipeline relies on a monolithic bundler that requires a full re-compilation of the entire dependency graph whenever a single UI component is modified, leading to significant developer idle time during local development.
solution: Transitioning the development environment to Vite leverages native ES modules to serve source files on-demand, bypassing the need for full-bundle regeneration during the development phase.
steps: Initialize a Vite project within the existing monorepo structure to serve as the new development orchestrator.
Configure the Vite dev server to proxy requests to the legacy backend API endpoints.
Implement Vite-specific plugins to handle legacy module resolution and TypeScript transpilation.
Replace the legacy dev script with the Vite CLI to enable instant Hot Module Replacement for UI components.
outcome: Developers experience near-instant feedback loops when modifying UI components, significantly reducing context switching and improving the daily development velocity.
limitation: Vite's reliance on native ESM can lead to inconsistencies between the development environment and the production build if legacy dependencies are not properly pre-bundled or if they rely on non-standard CommonJS patterns that require specific plugin configuration to resolve.
